name: Cudo – Protección de envíos
author: cudoecommerse

sections.description:
Cudo adds a shipping protection option to your cart or checkout. The customer chooses it (it is never pre-selected). If the package arrives damaged, gets lost or is stolen, the customer files a claim on your claims portal and Cudo compensates them.

  • You set the price: a percentage of the order, a fixed amount or price ranges.
  • Cudo deducts a fee from your Cudo balance for every protected order.
  • Works with the classic and the block-based cart and checkout.
  • Orders in Mexican pesos (MXN) from the minimum set in your Cudo account ($100 MXN by default).

The plugin’s interface is in Spanish (Mexico), the market Cudo operates in.

You need a Cudo account: https://app.cudo.lat/register

External service

This plugin connects to Cudo (https://cudo.lat), operated by SOS Soluciones Avanzadas S. de R.L. de C.V.:

  • When you sign in and while you use the admin pages: your account, balance, prices, brand kit, claims portal, protections, claims and transactions.
  • When a customer pays an order with protection: the order number and value, the products (name, quantity, price and image) and a SHA-256 hash of the customer’s email. The name, address, phone number and plain email are never sent.
  • When you assign a tracking number or cancel the order: the tracking number or the cancellation.
  • Extended warranty (only if Cudo enabled it for your account and you turned it on): when a customer pays an order with a warranty, the order number and date, the covered product (name, SKU, price, quantity and image), the plan chosen and what the customer paid for it, and the customer’s name and email, so Cudo can email them the code that activates their warranty in the Cudo app. Address and phone number are never sent. If the order is cancelled or refunded, the cancellation is sent too; if only a warranty line is refunded, only that warranty is cancelled. Once a day the plugin asks Cudo whether your account still has the warranty enabled (no customer data is sent).
  • When you use Tools → Export / Erase Personal Data for an email: a SHA-256 hash of that email, so Cudo can export or erase the name and email it keeps for warranties.
  • If you turn on address validation (shipping to Mexico only): while the customer types the address at checkout, the text typed in the address field and, when the address is complete, the street, neighborhood, city, state and postal code (never the name, email or phone). The store’s server sends them to Cudo, which checks them with Google Maps Platform (https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms); the customer’s browser never calls Cudo or Google. If an order is paid with an address that could not be confirmed and you turned on email notifications: the order number, its admin URL, that address, your store name and the email you chose, so Cudo can email you.
  • If you turn on estimated delivery (shipping within Mexico only): when a visitor sees the widget on a product page, the cart or the checkout, your origin postal code and preparation days, the visitor’s postal code (typed by them, taken from the checkout shipping address or resolved from their location), and the weight, dimensions and value of the product or cart, so Cudo can quote the delivery time with its carrier account (Skydropx, https://www.skydropx.com) and return the estimated date; Cudo completes the city and state of both postal codes with Google Maps Platform. If the visitor allows the browser to share their location, the coordinates (rounded to about 11 m) are sent once so Cudo can resolve their postal code with Google Maps Platform (https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms); if they do not, they can type it. The postal code is kept in the visitor’s browser (localStorage). The store’s server makes these requests and caches each route for one hour; the visitor’s browser never calls Cudo, Skydropx or Google. No name, email, phone or street address is sent.
  • The Brand Kit and claims portal screens preview the fonts you can choose for your portal; those previews load from Google Fonts. The plugin’s own interface font (Poppins, SIL Open Font License) is bundled.

Terms and conditions: https://www.cudo.lat/terminos-y-condiciones
Privacy notice: https://www.cudo.lat/aviso-de-privacidad
sections.installation:
1. Upload the .zip under Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin and activate it.
  2. Go to WooCommerce → Cudo and sign in with your Cudo account.
  3. Set your prices and turn the widget on.
sections.faq:
Where do I enter the tracking number?

In the order, under “Número de guía (Cudo)”. If you use WooCommerce Shipment Tracking or Advanced Shipment Tracking, it is taken from there.

What happens if I cancel an order?

The protection is cancelled and Cudo refunds the fee to your balance, unless 24 hours have passed since a real tracking number was assigned.

Which currencies are supported?

Only Mexican pesos (MXN). The widget stays hidden for any other currency.
sections.changelog:
0.4.0

  • New: Estimated delivery (Cudo → Entrega estimada, shipping within Mexico only). Shows “Llega el mié 6 nov” on the product page (below the variations), in the cart and in the checkout summary, in the classic and block-based versions. You set the origin postal code, the preparation days, where it appears and its colors. The visitor’s postal code comes from their browser, the checkout shipping address, their location (if they allow it) or what they type, and is shared across product, cart and checkout. It never slows the page or blocks the purchase: if the date cannot be calculated, or the package is not a parcel (over 1000 kg or 500 cm per side), nothing is promised.
  • New: Protection rules (Cudo → Protection rules). “Protect automatically”: chosen products or categories (Simple) or conditions that must all match (Advanced: product type, price, category, brand, tag). Those orders are protected without the customer turning it on and without charging them (your business pays it). “Exclude products”: with one of them in the cart the protection is not offered (exclusion wins). A cart with “always protected” and other products protects only the “always protected” ones and still offers the widget for the rest. Orders below the minimum are not auto-protected.
  • New: Address validation at checkout (shipping to Mexico only). When the customer stops typing, one notice lists what does not match (for example a postal code from another city) and suggests the corrected address; “Use address” fills it in without erasing what was typed. If Cudo has no suggestion, up to 3 similar addresses from the same city or postal code are shown. It never blocks the purchase.
  • New: Product → Shipping protection lets you set the name, description and image of the protection line, like the Shopify app.
  • Extended warranty: the switch text and the default product description no longer promise anything about the manufacturer’s warranty. The old default description is updated automatically, in the settings and in the hidden product.
  • Admin: uses the full screen width, tables become cards on mobile, every tab has its title and Home shows the status of every module.
  • Compatibility: the delivery and warranty widgets take their own row on variable products and in themes with an inline add-to-cart form; the address notice buttons keep their design in Hello Elementor, Neve and Astra.

0.3.0

  • New: extended warranty. Once Cudo enables it for your account, customers can add a 1 to 24 month plan to a product, on the product page or in a pop-up when adding it to the cart. You set the plans and prices and keep the margin; Cudo covers the claims and emails the customer an activation code.
  • Eligible products: all, chosen products and categories (subcategories included), or advanced rules by product type, price, category, brand and tag, plus exclusions.
  • New Product section: name (with the covered product’s name), description and image of the warranty line, shown in the classic and block cart and checkout, the mini cart and the order.
  • One warranty per product line: choosing another plan replaces the previous one, and it never covers more units than the product.
  • Coverage starts when the customer activates the warranty in the Cudo app with the emailed code plus the product’s serial number or SKU (the SKU is sent with every line); Cudo charges your account at that moment. Nothing is promised “until ” before activation.
  • Cudo only covers products within a price range (by default $50 to $10,000 MXN, set per account): products outside it are not offered a warranty, on the product page, in the pop-up or in the cart. No plan is preselected; the pop-up’s confirm button is disabled until a plan is chosen.
  • Refunding a whole warranty line cancels that warranty in Cudo; cancelling or fully refunding the order cancels them all (partial quantity refunds change nothing). Warranty lines added from the order admin are recognized too.
  • Tools → Export / Erase Personal Data ask Cudo for the warranty customer data, and show an error if Cudo cannot be reached.
  • Cudo requests that answer “too many requests” (429) are retried instead of logged as an issue.
  • The minimum order amount to offer the protection now comes from your Cudo account (by default $100 MXN) instead of a fixed $500 MXN.
  • The widget keeps its own button colors and switch design in themes that restyle every button or checkbox (Twenty Twenty-One, Astra, Hello Elementor, Sydney, OceanWP).
  • Admin: the Cudo menu wraps into two rows and keeps the active tab in view; the per-order fee is no longer shown in Home and Finance.

0.2.0

  • WooCommerce is now sent as the integration channel for the backend.
  • The store identity is sent as the real WooCommerce store URL.
  • Development defaults use the WooCommerce channel.

0.1.1

  • Security: the SVG cleaner for brand and portal images now also removes namespaced attributes and CSS escapes.
  • The protection is no longer offered when the store is signed out of Cudo, so customers are never charged for a protection that cannot be created.
  • A retry and an order status change can no longer send the same protection twice.
  • A cancelled order that is reactivated is protected again.
  • An unexpected response from Cudo shows a retry notice instead of breaking the admin page.
  • Tested with WooCommerce 11.2.

0.1.0

  • First release.

short_description: Your customers protect their shipment against damage, loss and theft when they pay. Cudo compensates them and you keep what you charged.
